note: No general-format / syntax-skeleton figure appears on any page of this batch. PDF printed pages 434-447 (OCCURS general rules, PAGE general rules, PICTURE syntax+general rules) are continuous prose and numbered rule lists only; the OCCURS and PICTURE general-format diagrams fall on the adjacent pages 463, 468 and 471, which are not in this batch. The choice-indicator (5.2.6.4 vertical-bar) defect class therefore had no surface to appear on here. Both findings below are cosmetic transcription-convention outliers, not normative losses.

findings.why_it_matters: In the PDF, 'FORMAT 4' at the foot of printed page 436 is an ordinary body-weight paragraph label, typographically identical to 'FORMAT 1' / 'FORMAT 2' / 'FORMAT 3' (which the transcription correctly renders as plain text on pages 464, 465, 472, 474 and 475). Promoting it to an H2 injects a spurious document-structure heading at exactly the same level as the '## Page N' navigational scaffolding, so any heading-driven TOC, outline or section-extraction over ISO_COBOL.md gains a bogus 'FORMAT 4' section and the true clause boundary is mis-anchored. It is also internally inconsistent: only 8 of the ~200 'FORMAT n' labels in the file are promoted this way.
findings.suggested_repair: Replace the line '## FORMAT 4' with the plain line 'FORMAT 4', matching how FORMAT 1/2/3 are transcribed on the surrounding pages. Sweep the other 7 '^#+\s*FORMAT \d' occurrences in specs/ISO_COBOL.md for the same defect.

findings.why_it_matters: All six 'integer-N' references on this page use U+2011 instead of the ASCII hyphen the PDF prints. The immediately preceding page (469), part of the same clause 13.18.39.4 General rules, uses ASCII hyphens for the identical terms. A grep or citation lookup for 'integer-7' therefore finds general rules 3)c) and 3)d) on page 469 but silently misses general rule 3)e) on page 470 - a retrieval hole in the one document this project treats as the authority for correct behavior. Verified by codepoint dump: the character at that position is decimal 8209.
findings.suggested_repair: Normalize U+2011 to U+002D throughout the page-470 slice. There are 107 U+2011 characters in specs/ISO_COBOL.md overall against thousands of ASCII hyphens; sweep them all in one pass so no normative term is unreachable by exact-match search.
